learning_outcomes.text: Sees the purpose and operational plan of the course, grasps the definition of language and its place in human life, knows the differences between spoken and written language.
Grasps the characteristics of language, the relationship between language-society and language-culture; knows reading and comprehension methods.
Knows the structure of the Turkish language and its place among language families in the world, the distinction between dialect-accent-mouth; understands the use of punctuation marks.
Sees the prominent works in the historical development of the Turkish language, knows the spelling rules.
Knows the sound features of the Turkish language, understands what culture is and its changing and unchanging elements.
Knows the derivational and inflectional suffixes of the Turkish language, grasps the characteristics of the poetry genre with examples. Sees the technology-language relationship.
Knows word types, grasps the characteristics of novel and short story with examples.
Knows word phrases, learns methods of preparing assignments-projects; grasps the characteristics of classical fictional genres such as fairy tales, fables, masnavi.
Knows the elements of the sentence and sentence types, gains information about functional texts such as theater and screenplay, sees the preliminary preparations for writing.
Grasps the characteristics of paragraph and text, knows functional genres such as article and critique.
Knows the semantic characteristics of words, knows functional genres such as essay and anecdote, sees communication errors in daily life with examples.
Gains information about idioms, proverbs and the vocabulary of the Turkish language, identifies expression disorders with examples.
Knows the current problems of the Turkish language, grasps the principles of effective and good speaking.
Recognizes scientific writings, sees examples of effective and good speaking.
Sees common communication errors, knows the intricacies of public speaking.

syllabus_topics: A. Purpose and operation of the course, definition of language and its place in human life B. Differences between spoken and written language.
A. Characteristics of language and grasping the structure of language. Reading and comprehension methods B. Punctuation marks
A. Turkish among world languages; differences between dialect, accent, and regional speech B. Grasping the language-thought relationship, critical thinking. Punctuation marks
A. Evaluation of major Turkish works B. Spelling rules
A. Sound features of Turkish with examples B. Changing and unchanging elements of culture
A. Examination of word structure in Turkish B. Poetry as a genre of writing and poetry analysis C. Preparations for writing D. Formal writing: petition, minutes, report...
A. Word types B. Novel and short story genres. Distinction between fiction and experience in literature. C. Dictionary usage
A. Word phrases B. Classical fictional genres C. Preparing assignments, projects D. Language errors in written and visual media
A. Sentence structure and sentence types in Turkish B. Functional texts: Theater, screenplay C. Principles of scientific writing. Planning in writing, how to make a good plan?
A. Supra-sentence language structures: paragraph and text B. Functional genres: Article-Critique. The problem of method in criticism. C. Communication accidents
A. Semantic knowledge B. Functional genres: Essay - Anecdote - Newspaper Column - Interview C. Paragraph writing; types and characteristics of paragraphs
A. Rhetorical arts and the vocabulary of Turkish B. Functional genres: Letter, Travelogue, Memoir, Diary. C. Language errors (expression disorders).
A. Current problems of Turkish B. Points to consider in diction C. Scientific writings
assessment_rules: The overall assessment is based on term work (40%) and a final exam (60%). Term work consists of three quizzes weighted at 30%, 30%, and 40% respectively. The final grade is calculated as 40% of the term work average plus 60% of the final exam score.
